newsitem.title: USA: Sacramento, Calif., divided on funding sports - poll.
newsitem.headline: Sacramento, Calif., divided on funding sports - poll.

text.p: Sacramento residents are evenly divided in their support of using public money to keep professional sports teams in the city, according to a poll commissioned by the Sacramento Bee newspaper.
The poll, published on Friday in the Bee, showed majority support of 51 percent for the idea of using public money to keep sports teams in town.
But when asked specifically about a possible Sacramento Kings basketball team deal using public money, the numbers turned, with 71 percent opposed and 27 percent in favor.

"It's a pretty scathing referendum on the public's feelings on the Kings' deal in particular," said Bob Kaufman, whose San Francisco firm, Minute Poll, conducted telephone interviews Wednesday with 572 Sacramento city residents for the Bee. The poll had a margin of error of 3.7 to 4.1 percentage points.

Earlier this month, Sacramento Kings owner Jim Thomas had asked the city to help him pay off his debt at the Arco Arena and to help build a new sports and entertainment complex. Without a financial commitment from city officials, he warned that he might be forced to move the team to another city.
